0 Pinochle Bezique Pinochle is a trick-taking game for 2 to 4 players. Players score points by melding cards in hand and playing tricks. This implementation supports 2-player Pinochle, single deck Pinochle, double deck Pinochle, and Bezique. Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Note that the BoardGameArena rules of 4 player Pinochle only allow card passing between partners in 'Friendly Mode'. You must select 'Card Exchange' as an option. If you are not playing friendly mode with card exchange, then in single deck partnership Pinochle, instead of passing cards, the declarer will pick up a 4 card kitty and discard 4 cards before declaring melds. [Rating: 2/10] Smell the nostalgia in the higher ratings. I find it the worst of the classic card games. The meld points are simply luck of the draw. Memorize loads of scoring rules. Restrict the card play during the tricks. Wow, how fun.

[Rating: 2/10] It's like Euchre or Bridge without the strategy.  The restrictions on card play can lead the game to practically play itself.  The rules lawyer element also grates on me.  The least enjoyable cards game I've played since Mao.

[Rating: 2/10] Double Deck Pinochle. All the worst of arcane trick-taking games: bombastic all-honour deck (hey I got six aces but so does everyone else); fancy scoring combinations (where cards can go in multiple ones but sometimes not); being doubly rewarded for lucky deals (melds and tricks); putting your cards on the table, then scooping them up again to play the hand (how's that for hidden but trackable information); enforced plays (yo partner, I'm really happy for you, I'mma let you finish but I'm trumping your high card). [Rating: 3/10] I do own two Pinochle decks as needed by the version I'm used to playing. I've not played in years and it's not the first game I'd propose.

[Rating: 3/10] Blech.  Twice I have played this in my lifetime and I can't stand the bidding code.  It just seems inane to me.  I'll never play Bridge for this reason, either.

[Rating: 3/10] Wow. What's the point? It's pieces of Rummy and a trick-taking game with a shout-out to Hearts without retaining the core essence of any of these games. Luck is huge on the melding, and putting your cards out there isn't much of a disadvantage. There might be some tricks to the trick-taking, but not much. This is mostly about knowing the scoring system, and that's about it. Boring.

[Rating: 3/10] Overview: 4p partnership trick-taker in which highest bidding side decides trump and switches out 4 cards. Points are scored for making the bid, showing melds, and taking Ace, 10, and Kings (modern scoring).  What I like: - Two 24 card decks. I feel that having two cards of each rank and suit leads to some interesting decisions compared to the normal decks.  What I dislike: - Pretty one sided bidding in which having runs in a suit or four aces already provide a lot of points.
